name: c2pa-ts
role: Pure TypeScript C2PA manifest reader and validator
summary: Pure TypeScript C2PA library (npm @trustnxt/c2pa-ts) that reads and validates Content Credentials in Node or browsers without native binaries, and can create manifests. Pre-1.0; chain-of-trust validation is not implemented.
use_when: Read or validate C2PA manifests in-process from a Node or browser pipeline
Avoid shelling out to a native CLI for manifest readback
avoid_when: Need a trust verdict on the signer: it reported a development signer as trusted; use c2patool
Need GIF, TIFF, WebP or JPEG XL assets: not supported
license: Apache-2.0 (project code, read from the 0.14.1 npm tarball).
notes: 2026-11-27: Lead said 0.14.1 and Apache-2.0; both match npm. Supported assets per README: JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, MP3, MP4; targets C2PA spec 2.1.
2026-11-27: Needs `import 'reflect-metadata'` before any c2pa-ts import under Node (tsyringe), documented in its README.
2026-11-27: Custom (unknown) assertions have no typed payload; read the CBOR box via assertion.sourceBox.contentBoxes.

2026-11-27: Predeclared check failed: for a c2patool development-signed PNG, c2pa-ts emitted signingCredential.trusted (success) where c2patool reports the signer untrusted. Never treat c2pa-ts trust codes as a trust verdict.

assessment.rationale: Apache-2.0 pure TypeScript C2PA reader, validator and creator with Node and browser support, pre-1.0 and small. Reads manifests c2patool produced, but its trust reporting differs from c2patool's, so c2patool stays the choice for trust questions; use c2pa-ts only where an in-process JS route is needed.

evidence.result: Read a 65 KB c2patool-signed PNG: title, VCRFixture 1.0, exact org.contentauth.test payload, isValid true, claimSignature.validated. KNOWN FAIL: signer reported trusted, not untrusted. Node 22.19.0.
evidence.scope: Node read and validate of one c2patool test-signed PNG; trust check failed (reported trusted); no signing, other formats, browser, or real signer.
